hints: Think about where you find each structure: root hairs are on plant root cells, microvilli are on animal gut lining cells. Which group has a cell wall?
Now picture one cell under the microscope: does a root hair cell grow one long extension, or many? Does an intestinal cell have one microvillus, or hundreds?
walkthrough:
**Sort plant versus animal**

Remember, root hairs belong to plants and microvilli belong to animals. That is your biggest clue.

Plant cells are surrounded by a cellulose cell wall, animal cells are surrounded only by a cell surface membrane.

**Decide who has the wall**

A root hair is just an extension of a plant root hair cell, so it is covered by cell wall plus membrane. A microvillus is a folding of an animal cell membrane, so it has no wall.

**Count how many per cell**

A root hair cell produces just one root hair to grow out into the soil. An epithelial cell in the ileum produces hundreds of tiny microvilli to increase surface area. So only microvillus fits more than one present on a cell.

options.A: Perfect match. Root hair is surrounded by cell wall (plant), and microvillus is present as many copies per cell (animal gut cell).
options.B: Microvilli are animal structures, so they are not surrounded by a cell wall, only by membrane.
options.C: A root hair cell has only one root hair, not more than one, so the second column is wrong.
options.D: Both columns are swapped. Microvilli have no wall and root hairs are single per cell.
